question: A factory records the production of two varieties of an article in three categories during two consecutive months. The first-month production is represented by $$A=\begin{bmatrix}80&60\\75&65\\90&85\end{bmatrix}$$ and the second-month production by $$B=\begin{bmatrix}90&50\\70&55\\75&75\end{bmatrix}.$$ Determine the combined production matrix and hence obtain the target production matrix if the factory plans production equal to $20\%$ more than this combined production, interpreting the entry in the second row and first column of the target matrix.
explanation:
Combined Production

Both $A$ and $B$ have order $3\times2$, so their addition is defined. The combined production is $$A+B=\begin{bmatrix}80&60\\75&65\\90&85\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}90&50\\70&55\\75&75\end{bmatrix}$$ $$=\begin{bmatrix}170&110\\145&120\\165&160\end{bmatrix}$$

Target Production

A production target $20\%$ above the combined production is $120\%$ of the combined matrix. Therefore, the target matrix is $$\frac{120}{100}(A+B)=\frac{6}{5}\begin{bmatrix}170&110\\145&120\\165&160\end{bmatrix}$$ $$=\begin{bmatrix}204&132\\174&144\\198&192\end{bmatrix}$$ This matrix also has order $3\times2$.

Interpretation

The entry in the second row and first column is $174$. Since rows represent the three categories and columns represent the two varieties, this entry means that the target production for the first variety in the second category is $174$ units. Hence, the required target production matrix is $\begin{bmatrix}204&132\\174&144\\198&192\end{bmatrix}$.

options.A: $A+B=\begin{bmatrix}170&110\\145&120\\165&160\end{bmatrix}$ and target $=\begin{bmatrix}204&132\\174&144\\198&192\end{bmatrix}$; the $(2,1)$ entry represents $174$ units
options.B: $A+B=\begin{bmatrix}170&110\\145&120\\165&160\end{bmatrix}$ and target $=\begin{bmatrix}204&132\\175&144\\198&192\end{bmatrix}$; the $(2,1)$ entry represents $175$ units
options.C: $A+B=\begin{bmatrix}170&110\\145&120\\165&160\end{bmatrix}$ and target $=\begin{bmatrix}136&88\\116&96\\132&128\end{bmatrix}$; the $(2,1)$ entry represents $116$ units
